gloss: New Year's soup with rice cakes

definitions.gloss: New Year's soup with rice cakes
definitions.explanation: A traditional Japanese soup eaten on New Year's Day, made with mochi (rice cakes) and various vegetables and proteins in a broth. Recipes vary significantly by region and family.

examples.japanese: お{正月|しょうがつ}に{雑煮|ぞうに}を{食|た}べる。
examples.english: We eat zōni on New Year's.

examples.japanese: うちの{雑煮|ぞうに}は{白|しろ}みそ{仕立|した}てだ。
examples.english: Our family's zōni is made with white miso.

examples.japanese: {雑煮|ぞうに}の{味|あじ}は{地域|ちいき}によって{大|おお}きく{異|こと}なり、{関東|かんとう}ではすまし{汁|じる}、{関西|かんさい}では{白|しろ}みそが{主流|しゅりゅう}だ。
examples.english: The taste of zōni varies greatly by region — clear broth is standard in Kantō, while white miso is the norm in Kansai.

notes:
CULTURE:
{雑煮|ぞうに} is one of the most important dishes of the Japanese New Year ({正月|しょうがつ}). It is traditionally eaten on the morning of January 1st. The recipe is deeply tied to regional and family identity — asking someone about their {雑煮|ぞうに} is a common conversation topic.

Regional variations include:
- {関東|かんとう}: clear broth (すまし{汁|じる}) with rectangular {餅|もち}
- {関西|かんさい}: {白|しろ}みそ broth with round {餅|もち}

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {雑煮|ぞうに}を{作|つく}る (to make zōni)
- {雑煮|ぞうに}を{食|た}べる (to eat zōni)
- お{雑煮|ぞうに} (zōni — with polite prefix お)
